topic: Agent identity / commerce / payments standards landscape (A2A, AP2, UCP, ACP, W3C/DIF, TEE attestation, execution receipts, BSC payment rails) — what AiKi must adapt to vs. must not duplicate
executive_summary:
The landscape moved substantially in the last 12 months and most of what is written about it in 2025-vintage material is now wrong. Five concrete corrections matter for AiKi.

(1) A2A shipped v1.0.0 (2026-03-12) and v1.0.1 (2026-05-28) under the Linux Foundation. AgentCard is now discovered at `/.well-known/agent-card.json`, transports are declared per-interface in `supported_interfaces[]` (`JSONRPC` | `GRPC` | `HTTP+JSON`), and cards are signed with detached JWS over RFC-8785-canonicalized JSON. Task lifecycle is 8 states + UNSPECIFIED. A2A is the transport/discovery layer; it has no identity root and no payments.

(2) AP2 v0.2 (2026-04-28) **threw away the Intent/Cart/Payment mandate trio** and the W3C-VC framing. It now defines exactly two mandates — Checkout Mandate (`vct: mandate.checkout.1` / `.open.1`) and Payment Mandate (`vct: mandate.payment.1` / `.open.1`) — as **SD-JWT VCs**, with a general "open mandate = user-signed constraint set + agent `cnf` key; closed mandate = agent-signed concrete instance" delegation model, delivered via OpenID4VP `transaction_data`. There is a fully specified constraint algebra (`payment.budget`, `payment.amount_range`, `payment.agent_recurrence`, `payment.allowed_payees`, `checkout.line_items`, …) and a Receipt type. AiKi should not invent a mandate schema; it should adopt this one.

(3) Google's **Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)** launched 2026-01-11 and is now the commerce layer AP2 secures; Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Salesforce and Stripe joined its Tech Council 2026-04-24. OpenAI/Stripe's ACP is still shipping (current API version `2026-04-17`) but is a competing, card-centric stack.

(4) For "execution receipts", **IETF SCITT is RFC 9943 and COSE Receipts is RFC 9942, both Proposed Standard, June 2026.** Combined with RATS (RFC 9334) + EAT (RFC 9711), the whole receipt/attestation vocabulary already exists. AiKi's Execution Receipt should be a profile of these, not a new format.

(5) The BSC payment-rail question resolves badly and I verified it on-chain (chainId 0x38): **BSC USDT `0x55d398…7955` and Binance-Peg USDC `0x8AC76a…580d` support neither EIP-3009 nor EIP-2612 permit** — every probe reverts with empty data. FDUSD and USD1 support both. Permit2 is live at the canonical address. This is a hard architectural constraint, not a preference.

findings.claim: A2A is at v1.0.1 (released 2026-05-28); v1.0.0 was 2026-03-12. It is a Linux Foundation project with 150+ supporting organizations and claimed production deployments.
findings.detail: GitHub releases for a2aproject/A2A: v1.0.1 published 2026-05-28T11:34:36Z; v1.0.0 published 2026-03-12T16:34:41Z; prior line was v0.3.0 (2025-07-30), v0.2.6, v0.2.5. The a2a-protocol.org spec page states "Latest Released Version: 1.0.0". Linux Foundation press release dated 2026-04-09 states: over 150 organizations (up from 50+ in April 2025), named adopters AWS, Cisco, Google, IBM, Microsoft, Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow; "active production deployments across multiple industries"; core repo >22,000 GitHub stars; SDKs in Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, .NET. Same release states AP2 is supported by 60+ organizations.

findings.claim: The A2A AgentCard is discovered at `/.well-known/agent-card.json` and its exact field set is defined in a2a.proto; JSON serialization is protojson (lowerCamelCase).
findings.detail: From specification/a2a.proto at tag v1.0.1, message AgentCard fields (field number, REQUIRED marker): name=1 REQUIRED, description=2 REQUIRED, supported_interfaces=3 REQUIRED (repeated AgentInterface), provider=4, version=5 REQUIRED, documentation_url=6 optional, capabilities=7 REQUIRED, security_schemes=8 (map<string,SecurityScheme>), security_requirements=9 (repeated), default_input_modes=10 REQUIRED, default_output_modes=11 REQUIRED, skills=12 REQUIRED, signatures=13 (repeated AgentCardSignature), icon_url=14 optional. AgentInterface = {url REQUIRED, protocol_binding REQUIRED ("The core ones officially supported are `JSONRPC`, `GRPC` and `HTTP+JSON`"), tenant, protocol_version REQUIRED}. AgentCapabilities = {streaming, push_notifications, extensions[], extended_agent_card}. AgentExtension = {uri, description, required, params}. AgentCardSignature = {protected (base64url JWS protected header), signature (base64url), header (Struct)}. Spec section 14.3 registers the well-known URI suffix `agent-card.json`; example: `https://agent.example.com/.well-known/agent-card.json`. NOTE: the normative sample card in docs/specification.md §8.5 serializes the security-requirements field as `"security"`, not `"securityRequirements"` — the proto contains no json_name override, so this is a discrepancy between prose sample and proto that an implementer must resolve against a real server.

findings.claim: A2A AgentCard signing is detached JWS over RFC 8785 canonical JSON with default-valued properties removed and `signatures` excluded.
findings.detail: docs/specification.md §8.4.3 Signature Verification, verbatim steps: "1. Extract the signature from the `signatures` array 2. Retrieve the public key using the `kid` and `jku` (or from a trusted key store) 3. Remove properties with default values from the received Agent Card 4. Exclude the `signatures` field 5. Canonicalize the resulting JSON using RFC 8785 6. Verify the signature against the canonicalized payload". Example protected header decodes to {"alg":"ES256","typ":"JOSE","kid":"key-1","jku":"https://example.com/agent/jwks.json"}. Clients SHOULD verify at least one signature before trusting a card; multiple signatures MAY be present for key rotation.

findings.claim: A2A task lifecycle is 9 enum values (8 meaningful states), with 4 terminal and 2 interrupted states.
findings.detail: enum TaskState from a2a.proto v1.0.1, verbatim with comments: TASK_STATE_UNSPECIFIED=0; TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED=1; TASK_STATE_WORKING=2; TASK_STATE_COMPLETED=3 (terminal); TASK_STATE_FAILED=4 (terminal); TASK_STATE_CANCELED=5 (terminal); TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED=6 (interrupted); TASK_STATE_REJECTED=7 (terminal); TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED=8 (interrupted).

findings.claim: A2A extensions are negotiated per-request via the `A2A-Extensions` HTTP header, and advertised in AgentCapabilities.extensions[] by URI. This is the hook AP2 and UCP both use.
findings.detail: docs/specification.md §14.2.2 "A2A-Extensions Header": "The A2A-Extensions header field contains a comma-separated list of extension URIs that the client wants to use for the request. Extensions allow agents to provide additional functionality beyond the core A2A specification while maintaining backward compatibility." AgentExtension carries {uri, description, required:bool, params:Struct}. UCP's A2A binding requires businesses to send `X-A2A-Extensions` with the UCP extension URI `https://ucp.dev/{version}/specification/reference`, plus a `UCP-Agent: profile="<uri>"` header.

findings.claim: AP2 v0.2 (published 2026-04-28) REPLACED the Intent/Cart/Payment mandate model with Checkout Mandate + Payment Mandate, and replaced W3C Verifiable Credentials with SD-JWT VCs. Any AiKi design based on 2025 AP2 writeups is building against a dead schema.
findings.detail: ap2-protocol.org sitemap lastmod 2026-04-28 for all pages; GitHub release v0.2.0 published 2026-04-28T12:40:54Z (previous release v0.1.0, 2025-09-16). Spec title verbatim: "Agentic Payment Protocol (v0.2)". Verbatim: "AP2 defines two Mandate types: Checkout Mandate and Payment Mandate." Mandate versioning: "Each AP2 Mandate type identifies its schema using the `vct` claim. The `vct` value includes a numeric suffix that acts as a schema version number (e.g. `mandate.payment.1`, `mandate.checkout.open.1`). Implementations MUST match the exact `vct` string, including the version suffix." Five roles: Shopping Agent (SA), Credential Provider (CP), Merchant (M), Merchant Payment Processor (MPP), Trusted Surface (TS). Verbatim scope statement: "AP2 operates as a security feature within a Commerce Protocol… AP2 is designed explicitly to be compatible with the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and integrates seamlessly." The AP2 python samples now key A2A DataParts as `ap2.mandates.PaymentMandateSdJwt` and `ap2.mandates.CheckoutMandateSdJwt` (previously `ap2.mandates.CartMandate`), plus `ap2.PaymentReceipt`; DEFAULT_MANDATE_TTL_SECONDS = 60*60.

findings.claim: AP2 defines a general open/closed mandate delegation model that is exactly the 'mandate' primitive AiKi wants — and it is protocol-agnostic by construction, not payment-specific.
findings.detail: From the Agent Authorization Framework page, verbatim: "AP2 makes use of this model for the payments use case, but the model could be applied more generally in the future." Two steps: Mandate Delegation (user approves Mandate Content on a Trusted Surface, receives a Mandate) and Action Authorization (Verifier challenges Agent; Agent presents Mandate; Verifier returns a Receipt). Two trust anchors are specified: (a) User Credential model — an external Issuer that Verifiers trust, delegation performed via OpenID4VP `transaction_data` with a `{type:"delegate", format, delegate_payload[], delegate_disclosures[]}` object, `delegate_payload` MUST be included in the Key Binding; (b) Trusted Agent Provider model — no pre-issued credential; the Agent Provider is trusted directly by Verifiers. Open mandate (`mandate.*.open.1`): user-signed, carries `constraints[]` + `cnf.jwk` (agent public key) + `iat`/`exp`; spec says "It is RECOMMENDED to set the `exp` claim for these Mandates to the smallest value that will allow the Shopping Agent to complete the assigned task." Closed mandate (`mandate.*.1`): agent-signed concrete instance (typ `kb+sd-jwt`, with `aud`, `nonce`, `sd_hash`). Anti-replay rule verbatim: "Shopping Agents MUST NOT present any subsequent open Payment or Checkout Mandates without receiving a rejection receipt from the previous one." Privacy rule: agents MUST present only the disclosures needed for evaluation.

findings.claim: AP2's Payment Mandate constraint algebra already covers budget, spend rate, amount range, allowed payee, allowed instrument, allowed PISP, execution window, and chaining to a Checkout Mandate — with normative evaluation semantics.
findings.detail: Closed Payment Mandate schema fields: vct (required), transaction_id (required; base64url hash of checkout_jwt, hash alg = sd_hash alg or sha256), payee:Merchant (required), pisp:Pisp, payment_amount:Amount (required; ISO4217 currency + integer minor units, e.g. 27999 = $279.99), payment_instrument:PaymentInstrument (required), execution_date (ISO8601; absent = immediate), risk_data (map of risk signals from trusted surface), iat, exp. Constraint types with exact `type` identifiers: `payment.agent_recurrence` {frequency enum ON_DEMAND|DAILY|WEEKLY|BIWEEKLY|MONTHLY|QUARTERLY|ANNUALLY, max_occurrences}; `payment.allowed_payees` {allowed: Merchant[]}; `payment.allowed_payment_instruments` {allowed: PaymentInstrument[]}; `payment.allowed_pisps`; `payment.amount_range` {currency, max, min}; `payment.budget` {max, currency} — "Evaluating the budget requires tracking the total amount spent using this Payment Mandate… the requested amount plus the total sum of amounts from previously closed Payment Mandates MUST be less than or equal to `max`. After approval, the amount MUST be added to the accumulated total"; `payment.reference` {conditional_transaction_id} for chaining. Checkout constraints: `checkout.allowed_merchants`, `checkout.line_items` (with a normative maximal-flow matching algorithm over acceptable_items × quantity). Note an inconsistency in the published examples: `payment.amount_range` example uses `"max": 100.50` (decimal) while the closed mandate `payment_amount.amount` is integer minor units (19900) — treat minor units as canonical and validate.

findings.claim: AP2 defines Receipts (Checkout Receipt, Payment Receipt) as first-class signed objects bound by hash to the closed Mandate — this is the closest existing analogue to an AiKi 'Execution Receipt' in the commerce stack.
findings.detail: Payment Receipt schema: status:ReceiptStatus (required; enum Success|Error), iss (required), iat (required, Unix epoch), reference (required; "The hash of the closed Mandate that this receipt is binding to"), error, error_description, payment_id (required), psp_confirmation_id (only if Success), network_confirmation_id (only if Success). Checkout Receipt schema: status, iss, iat, reference, error, error_description, order_id (present iff Success). Normative: "Once the Merchant Payment Processor has accepted or rejected the Payment Mandate, a signed Payment Receipt MUST be returned to the Shopping Agent, Credential Provider, and possibly Networks." Cryptographic binding requirement: "the Checkout JWT MUST be signed using a digital signature scheme (e.g., ECDSA) and not a deterministic signature (e.g., Ed25519)" to prevent rainbow-table attacks on checkout_hash.

findings.claim: AP2 ships x402 as a first-class sample rail alongside cards and DPC (Digital Payment Credentials), in both Human-Present and Human-Not-Present modes.
findings.detail: The AP2 docs nav lists sample flows: "Human Present Cards", "Human Present x402", "Human Not Present Cards", "Human Not Present x402", "Digital Payment Credentials Android". The repo contains code/samples/python/src/common/x402_constants.py whose current contents target Base Sepolia only: DEFAULT_USDC_CONTRACT = "0x036CbD53842c5426634e7929541eC2318f3dCF7e", DEFAULT_RPC_URL = "https://sepolia.base.org", with Anvil/Hardhat default accounts for user/merchant/facilitator. There is no BSC/BNB-chain sample in the AP2 repo. PaymentInstrument.type values seen in spec examples: "card", "UPI", "dpc".

findings.claim: Google's Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) is the new commerce layer that AP2 secures. It launched 2026-01-11, is Apache-2.0 on GitHub, has dated releases, and by 2026-04-24 Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Salesforce and Stripe had joined its Tech Council.
findings.detail: Repo universal-commerce-protocol/ucp: Apache-2.0, 3,314 stars, pushed_at 2026-08-18. Dated releases: v2026-01-11, v2026-01-23, v2026-04-08. Co-developed with Shopify, Etsy, Wayfair, Target, Walmart; endorsed by Adyen, American Express, Best Buy, Flipkart, Macy's, Mastercard, Stripe, The Home Depot, Visa, Zalando (from Google Developers Blog / press coverage — this adopter list is MARKETING, not spec). Discovery model: businesses publish `/.well-known/ucp` containing `ucp.version`, `ucp.services` (per-transport entries with `transport` ∈ rest|mcp|a2a|embedded and `endpoint`), `ucp.capabilities` (namespaced ids like `dev.ucp.shopping.checkout`, `dev.ucp.shopping.ap2_mandate`) and `ucp.payment_handlers`. Platforms publish a platform profile at a URI they send in the `UCP-Agent` header. A2A binding endpoint is the business's `/.well-known/agent-card.json`. AP2 integration is a negotiated capability `dev.ucp.shopping.ap2_mandate` with `"extends": "dev.ucp.shopping.checkout"` and `config.vp_formats_supported: {"dc+sd-jwt": {}}`; once negotiated the session is "Security Locked" — "Neither party may revert to a standard (unprotected) checkout flow." All AP2 fields nest under a single `ap2` object, excluded from the business's signature canonicalization.

findings.claim: OpenAI/Stripe's ACP is alive and still shipping, currently at API version 2026-04-17, but it is a card/PSP-centric stack with no crypto rail and no agent-identity layer.
findings.detail: Repo agentic-commerce-protocol/agentic-commerce-protocol: Apache-2.0, 1,513 stars, pushed_at 2026-07-18. Dated spec versions in /spec: 2025-09-29, 2025-12-12, 2026-01-16, 2026-01-30, 2026-04-17. Changelog 2026-04-17 verbatim: "API Version: `2026-04-17`", "Previous version `2026-01-30` deprecated"; adds 3DS authentication outcome examples, multi-item checkout, and an unreleased push-model Feed API (POST /feeds, GET /feeds/{id}, GET/PATCH /feeds/{id}/products; metadata.json + products.jsonl). Delegated Payment Spec: single endpoint `POST /agentic_commerce/delegate_payment` (OpenAI → PSP), headers Authorization, Accept-Language, User-Agent, Idempotency-Key, Request-Id, Content-Type, Signature, Timestamp, API-Version. Request body: payment_method (required), allowance (required), billing_address, risk_signals (required), metadata (required). Allowance: {reason: enum currently only "one_time", max_amount:int minor units, currency: ^[a-z]{3}$ lowercase ISO-4217, checkout_session_id, merchant_id, expires_at RFC3339}. 201 response: {id, created RFC3339, metadata}. PaymentMethodCard requires {type:"card", card_number_type ∈ fpan|network_token, number, display_card_funding_type ∈ credit|debit|prepaid, metadata}. Note ACP allowance is strictly single-use one-time; it has nothing comparable to AP2's budget/recurrence constraint algebra.

findings.claim: ERC-8004 is still Draft (created 2025-08-13) and explicitly positions itself as the discovery/trust layer *below* A2A and MCP, with a registration file that references an A2A AgentCard by URL. This is the concrete A2A↔ERC-8004 convergence point — but the draft still pins A2A version "0.3.0".
findings.detail: ERC front matter verbatim: eip: 8004, title: Trustless Agents, authors Marco De Rossi (@MarcoMetaMask), Davide Crapis (@dcrapis, ethereum.org), Jordan Ellis (Google), Erik Reppel (Coinbase), status: Draft, type: Standards Track, category: ERC, created: 2025-08-13, requires: 155, 712, 721, 1271. Motivation verbatim: "MCP allows servers to list and offer their capabilities…, while Agent2Agent (A2A) handles agent authentication, skills advertisement via AgentCards, direct messaging, and complete task-lifecycle orchestration. However, these agent communication protocols don't inherently cover agent discovery and trust." The registration file `services[]` array includes an entry `{"name": "A2A", "endpoint": "https://agent.example/.well-known/agent-card.json", "version": "0.3.0"}` — stale relative to A2A 1.0.1. Also includes MCP (version "2025-06-18" — also stale; MCP is now 2026-07-28), OASF, ENS, DID, email, web. Top-level: `x402Support: false|true`, `active: bool`, `registrations[{agentId, agentRegistry:"{namespace}:{chainId}:{identityRegistry}"}]`, and OPTIONAL `supportedTrust: ["reputation","crypto-economic","tee-attestation"]` — verbatim: "If absent or empty, this ERC is used only for discovery, not for trust." Optional endpoint-domain verification via `https://{endpoint-domain}/.well-known/agent-registration.json`. Verbatim on payments: "Payments are orthogonal to this protocol and not covered here."

findings.claim: There is no formal convergence effort between the A2A AgentCard and the ERC-8004 registration file. They are complementary by reference, not merged: ERC-8004 links to a card, it does not embed or mirror its schema.
findings.detail: The ERC-8004 registration file has 4 top-level descriptive fields (type, name, description, image — explicitly "to ensure compatibility with ERC-721 apps") plus services/registrations/supportedTrust/x402Support/active. The A2A AgentCard has 14 fields dominated by capabilities, skills, securitySchemes, supportedInterfaces and JWS signatures. No field is shared beyond name/description. ERC-8004 says "The number and type of *endpoints* are fully customizable" and "The *version* field in endpoints is a SHOULD, not a MUST". Nothing in the A2A v1.0.1 spec or proto references ERC-8004, on-chain registries, or blockchain identity. Conclusion: the join key is a URL, and the only overlap risk is name/description drift between the two documents.

findings.claim: VERIFIED ON-CHAIN (BSC chainId 0x38, 2026-08-18): BSC USDT and Binance-Peg USDC support NEITHER EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization NOR EIP-2612 permit. FDUSD and USD1 support both. All four are 18 decimals.
findings.detail:
Method: eth_call against https://bsc-dataseed.bnbchain.org with zero-filled args; a function that exists reverts with an Error(string) reason, a function that does not exist falls through and reverts with empty data (0x).

0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 name="Tether USD" symbol=USDT decimals=18 — transferWithAuthorization: revert 0x; receiveWithAuthorization: revert 0x; permit: revert 0x; DOMAIN_SEPARATOR(): revert; nonces(): revert; authorizationState(): revert. NOT a proxy (EIP-1967 impl slot = 0x0). => NO 3009, NO 2612.
0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d name="USD Coin" symbol=USDC decimals=18 — identical all-empty reverts. EIP-1967 impl = 0xba5fe23f8a3a24bed3236f05f2fcf35fd0bf0b5c. => NO 3009, NO 2612.
0xc5f0f7b66764F6ec8C8Dff7BA683102295E16409 name="First Digital USD" symbol=FDUSD decimals=18, impl 0xa6b2c3d2910246fb0adb02e5f6b39e29026e6d50 — transferWithAuthorization: revert "Authorization expired"; receiveWithAuthorization: revert "Authorization expired"; permit: revert "ERC20Permit: expired deadline"; DOMAIN_SEPARATOR() = 0xac2ff863e00ee93e90d01514d46b9b8179ca650e856138a6d8aea00702ca62a0; nonces() and authorizationState() return 0. => EIP-3009 YES, EIP-2612 YES.
0x8d0D000Ee44948FC98c9B98A4FA4921476f08B0d name="World Liberty Financial USD" symbol=USD1 decimals=18, impl 0x694aa534bdef8ed63244eb902e7914e527891f08 — transferWithAuthorization: revert "EIP3009: authorization is expired"; receiveWithAuthorization: same; permit: "ERC20Permit: expired deadline"; version()=2; DOMAIN_SEPARATOR()=0x5d939dc193fd011c5e26fb861450a696546a09db6b26db26501fe354ba3ed4ba; eip712Domain() returns data; TRANSFER_WITH_AUTHORIZATION_TYPEHASH()=0xd099cc98ef71107a616c4f0f941f04c322d8e254fe26b3c6668db87aae413de8. => EIP-3009 YES, EIP-2612 YES.

Critical secondary fact: BSC USDT/USDC are 18 decimals, not 6 as on Ethereum/Base. Any amount math ported from an x402/Base implementation will be wrong by 10^12.

findings.claim: VERIFIED ON-CHAIN: Uniswap Permit2 is deployed on BSC at the canonical cross-chain address 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3 and is functional. This is the only universal gasless-authorization path for BSC USDT/USDC.
findings.detail: eth_getCode returns 9,153 bytes of runtime code at 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3 on chainId 0x38. DOMAIN_SEPARATOR() returns 0x4142cc3c823f819c467fa4437d637fe20589a31dfcd1da2ff22292c9ed9344e7. allowance(address,address,address) (selector 0x927da105) returns a 3-word tuple (amount uint160, expiration uint48, nonce uint48) — confirming the AllowanceTransfer interface. Permit2's SignatureTransfer path (permitTransferFrom with PermitTransferFrom{TokenPermissions{token,amount}, nonce, deadline}) works with ANY ERC-20 including USDT/USDC, but requires a ONE-TIME on-chain `approve(PERMIT2, max)` from the payer — i.e. it is gasless only after the first transaction, unlike EIP-3009 which is gasless from transaction zero.

findings.claim: Circle does not issue native USDC on BNB Smart Chain. The 0x8AC76a… token is Binance-Peg. Any assumption of Circle FiatTokenV2_2 semantics (6 decimals, EIP-3009, blocklist) on BSC is wrong.
findings.detail: Circle's multi-chain USDC materials list native issuance on Ethereum, Solana, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon PoS, Avalanche C-Chain, Stellar, Algorand, Hedera, Flow, Tron, Aptos, Sui, Sei, Noble, Polygon zkEVM as of mid-2026 — BNB Smart Chain is not among them. Circle has shipped other products on BNB Chain (USYC tokenized money-market fund), which is not the same as USDC issuance. Corroborated by the on-chain probe: the BSC USDC contract has 18 decimals and no FiatToken methods, which no Circle-issued USDC has.
findings.source_date: 2026 (Circle multi-chain page, exact revision date not captured)

findings.claim: 'Execution receipts' as a standard ALREADY EXISTS and is now Proposed Standard: IETF SCITT is RFC 9943 and COSE Receipts is RFC 9942, both June 2026. AiKi should profile these, not invent a format.
findings.detail: RFC 9943 "An Architecture for Trustworthy and Transparent Digital Supply Chains" (SCITT), Proposed Standard, June 2026. Definitions: a Signed Statement is "an identifiable and non-repudiable Statement about an Artifact signed by an Issuer", encoded as COSE_Sign1 (RFC 9052); a Receipt is a COSE Single Signer Data Object proving that a Signed Statement has been registered in a Transparency Service's Verifiable Data Structure; a Transparent Statement is a Signed Statement plus one or more Receipts, and "remains a valid Signed Statement and may be registered again in a different TS". Protected header carries alg, content type, kid, and CWT Claims (issuer, subject). RFC 9942 "CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) Receipts", Standards Track, June 2026, registers COSE header parameters 394 (`receipts`: array of Receipts), 395 (`vds`: verifiable data structure algorithm), 396 (`vdp`: verifiable data structure proofs by proof type), with CDDL: Receipt = Receipt_For_Inclusion / Receipt_For_Consistency, each #6.18(COSE_Sign1) over an RFC9162_SHA256 inclusion or consistency proof header.

findings.claim: For attestation-of-execution, the canonical vocabulary is RATS: RFC 9334 (architecture, Jan 2023) + RFC 9711 EAT (Proposed Standard, April 2025), with RFC 9781 (UCCS) and RFC 9782 (EAT media types) in May 2025.
findings.detail: RFC 9711 "The Entity Attestation Token (EAT)", Standards Track / Proposed Standard, published April 2025; it assumes familiarity with RFC 9334 "Remote ATtestation procedureS (RATS) Architecture" and uses its roles (Attester, Verifier, Relying Party) and concepts (Evidence, Attestation Results). RFC 9781 defines a CBOR tag for Unprotected CWT Claims Sets (May 2025); RFC 9782 defines EAT media types (May 2025). RATS also has an in-flight Conceptual Messages Wrapper draft (draft-ietf-rats-msg-wrap).

findings.claim: Agent-specific receipt/attestation standards exist only as individual Internet-Drafts and vendor proposals — none are adopted. This is a genuine gap AiKi could fill, but it should be filled as a SCITT/COSE profile.
findings.detail: draft-mih-agent-bilateral-attestation-01, "Bilateral Attestation of Cross-Organization Agent Actions", Steven Mih (Action State Group, Inc.), 19 July 2026, expires 20 January 2027 — an individual submission, explicitly not endorsed by IETF. It defines four structures: Request Attestation (requesting org signs the action's material terms: content digest, nonce, timestamp, validity window), Action Attestation (performing org signs a response referencing the request by digest, recording deterministic constraint-evaluation results and a disposition ∈ executed|blocked|denied|timeout|errored|deferred|expired|escalated), Acknowledgment (each party's signed receipt of the counterparty's attestation), and Constraint Records (pinned constraint-set digests, input-commitment digests, completeness requirements). Three asymmetry dispositions for failed exchanges: delivery_unconfirmed, counterparty_timeout, countersign_refused. Also in flight: draft-chueayen-attestation-receipts (Enforcement Attestation Receipts for AI Inference Decisions), draft-sirkkavaara-vaara-receipt-06, and Microsoft's agent-governance-toolkit "Independently Verifiable Compliance Receipts" proposal. All individual/vendor, none WG-adopted.

findings.claim: TEE attestation for agents is practical today and there is a working reference implementation binding Intel TDX attestation to an ERC-8004 agentId — Phala's erc-8004-tee-agent, with a TEE Registry extension contract.
findings.detail: Repo Phala-Network/erc-8004-tee-agent (pushed 2026-01-29): "An ERC-8004 Compliant TEE Agent with a TEE Registry Extension for Secure & Verifiable Trustless Agents in a CVM on Phala Cloud". Contracts: ITEERegistry.sol, TEERegistry.sol, DstackVerifier.sol, IAutomataDcapAttestation.sol, IAutomataDcapVerifier.sol, IdentityRegistry.sol. ITEERegistry defines a Key struct {bytes32 teeArch, bytes32 codeMeasurement, bytes pubkey, string codeConfigUri, address verifier} keyed by (agentId, pubkey), with addKey(agentId, teeArch, codeMeasurement, pubkey, codeConfigUri, verifier, proof) and an allowlist of on-chain verifiers by vendor. Stack: Intel TDX + NVIDIA H100 GPU TEE via Phala dstack (repo Dstack-TEE/dstack, actively pushed 2026-08-18, "Open framework for confidential AI"), TDX quote + RTMR evidence, verified on-chain by Automata's DCAP verifier. Automata DCAP v1.1 adds verifyAndAttestOnChain(bytes rawQuote, uint32 tcbEvalDataNumber), an AutomataTcbEvalDao for on-chain TCB recovery data, ZK paths (RISC Zero ImageID 0xcc80dc6c1c1f8bc524101b72b3900301dc87887457c8fcaf552e45e2a02b9695, SP1 VKEY 0x008228a87e56a065fb3ad27026aef08acc97d72d289439e8dab0d53baaea9f26), and claims ~1M gas reduction per on-chain DCAP quote verification.
findings.source_date: 2026-01-29 (Phala repo); 2026-08-18 (dstack); Automata v1.1 undated in NOTE.md

findings.claim: W3C is where the credential formats live, and they are done or nearly done: VC Data Model 2.0 is a Recommendation (15 May 2025); DID Core 1.1 is a Candidate Recommendation Snapshot (5 March 2026), not yet a Recommendation.
findings.detail: VC Data Model 2.0, status verbatim: "This document was published by the Verifiable Credentials Working Group as a Recommendation using the Recommendation track. W3C recommends the wide deployment of this specification as a standard for the Web." Date 15 May 2025. DID 1.1: "W3C Candidate Recommendation Snapshot", 05 March 2026, this-version URL https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CR-did-1.1-20260305/, "not expected to advance to Recommendation any earlier than 05 April 2026". DID Core 1.0 has been a Recommendation since 19 July 2022. DID Resolution 1.0 is at CR (https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CR-did-resolution-1.0-20260806/, 6 Aug 2026). Notably, AP2 v0.2 chose SD-JWT VC + OpenID4VP over W3C VC JSON-LD — so W3C VC 2.0 is NOT the format the commerce stack converged on.

findings.claim: DIF's Trusted AI Agents Working Group is the live standards venue for agent identity + delegation, centred on KYA-OS (donated by Vouched, March 2026). Output is reports and an MCP reference implementation, not yet a ratified spec.
findings.detail: DIF Trusted AI Agents WG active work items: delegated-authority-report, delegated-authority-threat-model, governance-of-delegated-authority-report, kya-os-mcp ("KYA-OS MCP protocol reference implementation — delegation, proof generation, session lifecycle, and cryptographic identity for the Model Context Protocol"), trusted-ai-agents / trusted-ai-agents-wg. KYA-OS Task Force meets weekly Tuesdays 09:00 ET. KYA-OS = "Know Your Agent Operating System"; uses DIDs + VCs to give agents verifiable identities and represent delegation as tamper-evident, explicitly-scoped credentials; defines three conformance levels. Scope stated as covering "the full range of agentic protocols", i.e. it is meant to sit across MCP and A2A.
findings.source_date: 2026 (WG page, exact revision undated); KYA-OS donated March 2026

findings.claim: MCP shipped a breaking redesign in spec version 2026-07-28: it is now stateless — no initialize handshake, no Mcp-Session-Id, no ping — with a new server/discover RPC and a Multi Round-Trip Request pattern. Any AiKi MCP adapter written against 2025-06-18 or 2025-11-25 is obsolete.
findings.detail: Spec versions present in the repo: 2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25, 2026-07-28. Major changes in 2026-07-28 (verbatim highlights): removal of protocol-level sessions and the `Mcp-Session-Id` header (SEP-2567); removal of the initialize/notifications-initialized handshake — every request carries `io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` and `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities` in `_meta` (SEP-2575); new `server/discover` RPC which servers MUST implement; `subscriptions/listen` replaces the HTTP GET endpoint and resources/subscribe; tasks moved out of core into extension `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks` with polling via tasks/get and tasks/update (SEP-2663); Multi Round-Trip Requests replace server-initiated roots/list, sampling/createMessage, elicitation/create — servers return `InputRequiredResult` with `resultType: "input_required"` and `inputRequests`, clients retry with `inputResponses` (SEP-2322); all results carry a required `resultType`; SSE resumability and Last-Event-ID removed. Minor: `extensions` field added to Client/ServerCapabilities; required `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` headers on Streamable HTTP POST; required `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` on list/read results (CacheableResult). Note: ERC-8004's registration file example still pins MCP version "2025-06-18".

findings.claim: Verifiable-inference (zkML) tooling is real but not production-grade for LLM-sized agent work; TEE attestation is the only practical near-term proof-of-execution.
findings.detail: EZKL latest release v23.0.5 (2026-02-20); prior v23.0.3 (2025-10-26). Lagrange DeepProve ("Framework to prove inference of ML models blazingly fast") 3,361 stars, last push 2026-05-31. Secondary sources report EZKL handling ONNX models up to ~50M parameters and DeepProve delivering 54–158× GPU-accelerated speedups via GKR — these figures come from analysis writeups, not from a benchmark I fetched from the projects themselves, so treat as indicative only. Contrast: Phala dstack + Automata DCAP verify a full TDX quote on-chain today with a documented ~1M gas reduction in v1.1, and Phala ships an ERC-8004-integrated TEE agent. TEE-based approaches (Phala, Automata, Atoma, Marlin Oyster, Ritual's TEE-EOVMT) are what actually ship; zkML remains restricted to small models.

interfaces.body:
; RFC 9942, "CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) Receipts"
; Standards Track, June 2026
;
; New COSE header parameters:
;   394  receipts : array of one or more COSE Receipts
;   395  vds      : algorithm identifier for the Verifiable Data Structure
;   396  vdp      : map of Verifiable Data Structure Proofs, keyed by Proof Type

Receipt = Receipt_For_Inclusion / Receipt_For_Consistency

Receipt_For_Inclusion   = #6.18(Signed_Inclusion_Proof)
Receipt_For_Consistency = #6.18(Signed_Consistency_Proof)

Signed_Inclusion_Proof = [
  protected   : bstr .cbor RFC9162_SHA256_Inclusion_Protected_Header,
  unprotected : RFC9162_SHA256_Inclusion_Unprotected_Header,
  payload     : bstr / nil,
  signature   : bstr
]

Signed_Consistency_Proof = [
  protected   : bstr .cbor RFC9162_SHA256_Consistency_Protected_Header,
  unprotected : RFC9162_SHA256_Consistency_Unprotected_Header,
  payload     : bstr / nil,
  signature   : bstr
]

; SCITT (RFC 9943, Proposed Standard, June 2026) layers on top:
;   Signed Statement     = COSE_Sign1 (RFC 9052) binding an Issuer to a Statement
;                          about an Artifact; protected header carries alg, content
;                          type, kid, and CWT Claims (issuer, subject)
;   Receipt              = proof that a Signed Statement was registered in a
;                          Transparency Service's Verifiable Data Structure
;   Transparent Statement = Signed Statement + one or more Receipts (label 394);
;                          "remains a valid Signed Statement and may be registered
;                          again in a different TS"

aiki_implications: DO NOT invent an AiKi mandate schema. Adopt AP2 v0.2's open/closed mandate model wholesale: `mandate.payment.open.1` / `mandate.payment.1`, `mandate.checkout.open.1` / `mandate.checkout.1`, SD-JWT VC encoding, `cnf.jwk` for agent key binding, `constraints[]` with the published `type` identifiers. It is the only standard with a real constraint algebra (budget + recurrence + payee allowlist + amount range + chaining) and it already declares itself protocol-agnostic ('the model could be applied more generally in the future'). Reinventing this costs you interop with Google, UCP, and every AP2 verifier for zero technical gain.

THE ONE PLACE AiKi ADDS REAL VALUE IN MANDATES: AP2's `payment.budget` evaluation is normatively stateful — 'Evaluating the budget requires tracking the total amount spent using this Payment Mandate... After approval, the amount MUST be added to the accumulated total for future evaluation.' AP2 specifies the rule but not the state store, so today every Verifier must keep its own private accumulator and no two Verifiers can share one. An on-chain BSC spend accumulator keyed by the open-mandate digest, that any Verifier can read and any Merchant can write to atomically with settlement, is a genuine, standards-compatible contribution. Build that. Same argument applies to `payment.agent_recurrence` occurrence counting and to the anti-replay rule ('MUST NOT present any subsequent open Mandates without receiving a rejection receipt from the previous one'), which is unenforceable without shared state.

DO NOT define a new Execution Receipt format. Profile RFC 9942 (COSE Receipts) + RFC 9943 (SCITT), both Proposed Standard as of June 2026. An AiKi Execution Receipt = a COSE_Sign1 Signed Statement whose CWT Claims issuer is the agent's ERC-8004 agentId (as a DID or eip155 CAIP identifier) and whose subject is the task digest; register it in an AiKi Transparency Service; return the RFC 9942 Receipt (header label 394) to the client. This buys you existing tooling, existing verifiers, and an argument to auditors. Inventing a bespoke JSON receipt buys you nothing and dates instantly.

BSC PAYMENT RAILS — THIS IS THE BLOCKER, AND IT IS CONFIRMED. BSC USDT (0x55d398...7955) and Binance-Peg USDC (0x8AC76a...580d) support NEITHER transferWithAuthorization NOR permit. Verified by eth_call: every probe reverts with empty data. Design consequence: you cannot build a gasless-from-first-transaction x402-style 'exact' scheme on the two most liquid BSC stablecoins. Your options are (a) restrict native EIP-3009 settlement to FDUSD and USD1, which both work; (b) route USDT/USDC through Permit2 SignatureTransfer at 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3 (confirmed live on BSC), accepting a one-time on-chain approve(PERMIT2, max) paid in BNB by every new payer; or (c) require ERC-4337 / EIP-7702 smart accounts with a paymaster and treat the EOA path as unsupported. Pick one now — this decision reaches into the onboarding UX, the fee model, and the settlement contract.

SECOND BSC LANDMINE: all four BSC stablecoins I probed are 18 decimals, not 6. Any x402 facilitator, Coinbase reference code, or AP2 sample ported from Base/Ethereum encodes amounts in 10^6. Porting it unchanged produces a 10^12 amount error. Bake the per-chain, per-token decimals into a config table and assert it in tests, and treat 'USDC means 6 decimals' as a forbidden assumption in the codebase.

A2A ADAPTER = serve a signed AgentCard at /.well-known/agent-card.json (14 fields; supportedInterfaces with protocolBinding JSONRPC|GRPC|HTTP+JSON; signatures[] as detached JWS with kid+jku over RFC-8785-canonicalized JSON minus defaults minus signatures), implement the 9-value TaskState machine, and register ONE AiKi extension URI advertised in capabilities.extensions[] and negotiated per-request via the `A2A-Extensions` header. That extension is where mandates, receipts, and settlement proof ride. Do not fork the AgentCard schema; do not add top-level fields.

ERC-8004 ADAPTER = the registration file's services[] array, with an entry {name:'A2A', endpoint:'<your agent-card URL>', version:'1.0.1'} — note the ERC's own example still says 0.3.0, so emit the correct version and expect indexers to be lenient. Set supportedTrust to the models you actually back. Use agentRegistry 'eip155:56:<address>' for BSC. Critically: ERC-8004 says 'Payments are orthogonal to this protocol and not covered here' — so payments/mandates/receipts are AiKi's lane, not a duplication. But ERC-8004 is still DRAFT (created 2025-08-13), so pin a schema version and expect churn.

THERE IS NO A2A↔ERC-8004 SCHEMA CONVERGENCE, and you should not wait for one. The two documents join by URL only — ERC-8004 links to an AgentCard, it does not mirror its fields. The practical risk is name/description drift between the on-chain registration file and the off-chain card. Fix it by making the registration file the source of truth and generating the AgentCard's name/description/iconUrl from it, or by cross-hashing: put the AgentCard's RFC-8785 digest in ERC-8004 on-chain metadata via setMetadata(agentId, 'a2aCardHash', ...). That last move is cheap and is a differentiator nobody else has shipped.

COMMERCE-LAYER STRATEGY: AiKi should adapt to AP2 (the security/mandate layer) and NOT try to be UCP or ACP. UCP has Google + Shopify + Amazon + Meta + Microsoft + Salesforce + Stripe on its Tech Council as of April 2026; ACP has OpenAI + Stripe and is on API version 2026-04-17. You will not win a commerce-protocol war and you do not need to — AP2 explicitly sits above any Commerce Protocol ('The exact details of the Commerce Protocol... are outside the scope of AP2'). Position AiKi as an AP2-compatible Credential Provider + Merchant Payment Processor for crypto rails, and expose a UCP capability `dev.ucp.shopping.ap2_mandate`-shaped surface if you want UCP merchants.

IF you also want ACP/OpenAI reach: implement POST /agentic_commerce/delegate_payment as a PSP. But note the semantic mismatch that will bite you — ACP's Allowance.reason enum currently permits only 'one_time', with no budget, recurrence, or payee allowlist. An AiKi standing mandate cannot be expressed in ACP. Model ACP as a strictly weaker, single-shot projection of an AiKi/AP2 mandate, and make the downgrade explicit in code rather than accidental.

TEE ATTESTATION IS PRACTICAL TODAY — copy Phala, do not build from scratch. ITEERegistry.sol already defines the exact shape: Key{teeArch, codeMeasurement, pubkey, codeConfigUri, verifier} keyed by (agentId, pubkey), with an allowlist of on-chain verifiers by vendor, and addKey(..., bytes proof) verifying an Intel TDX DCAP quote. Adopt that interface. BUT: verify that an Automata DCAP verifier is actually deployed on BNB Smart Chain before designing around on-chain quote verification — I could not confirm this, and if it is absent you must either deploy it yourself (non-trivial: it needs on-chain PCCS collateral + TCB recovery data upkeep) or fall back to an off-chain verifier oracle that signs attestation results.

zkML IS NOT READY for agent-scale execution proofs. EZKL's last release was 2026-02-20 and is bounded to small ONNX models; Lagrange DeepProve is the fastest option and still targets ML inference, not arbitrary agent execution. Do not put verifiable-inference proofs on the critical path of an Execution Receipt. Structure the receipt so the proof is a pluggable attachment — {tee-attestation | crypto-economic re-execution | zkml | none} — mirroring ERC-8004's supportedTrust enum, and ship with TEE attestation and reputation only.

IDENTITY FORMAT: do NOT build on W3C VC 2.0 JSON-LD just because it is a Recommendation. The commerce stack converged on SD-JWT VC + OpenID4VP (AP2 v0.2, UCP's vp_formats_supported: {'dc+sd-jwt': {}}). Use SD-JWT VC as the credential format and reserve DIDs for the ERC-8004 services[] DID entry. DID Core 1.1 is still only a Candidate Recommendation (5 March 2026), so do not depend on 1.1-only features.

WATCH DIF's Trusted AI Agents WG / KYA-OS but do not block on it. It is producing reports (delegated-authority-report, threat model, governance) and an MCP reference implementation, not a ratified spec. If AiKi ships an on-chain mandate accumulator and a SCITT-profiled execution receipt, contributing that to the KYA-OS Task Force is a cheap standards-credibility play — the WG meets weekly and has no on-chain settlement story.

REFRESH YOUR MCP ADAPTER. Spec version 2026-07-28 is a breaking redesign: no initialize handshake, no Mcp-Session-Id, no ping, mandatory server/discover, mandatory resultType on every result, tasks moved to the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension, and the Multi Round-Trip Request pattern replacing server-initiated requests. Anything targeting 2025-06-18 or 2025-11-25 is obsolete. Note also that MCP's per-request _meta and the new `extensions` capability field give you a clean place to carry AiKi mandate/receipt references without forking the protocol.
